chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, both together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who was found killed, and it was not known who killed him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was known and he had guardians seeking his blood money, they would be given his blood money from the treasury of the Muslims, and the blood of a Muslim man would not be invalidated, because his inheritance is for the Imam (peace be upon him). Thus, his blood money is upon the Imam, and they pray over him and bury him.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And he ruled regarding a man who was crushed by the people on Friday in the throng of the people, so he died, that his blood money is from the treasury of the Muslims.'

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money / compensation for death or injury

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the blood money of a Muslim whose killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'bayt al-mal' assuming financial liability for the blood money of a 'maktum al-qatil' (unknown killer), ensuring no Muslim's blood is left unpaid. It highlights the Imam's dual role as both spiritual leader and judicial heir, extending this protection to accidental deaths like crowd crushing, thereby reinforcing the concept of communal responsibility in Shia jurisprudence.
